title: MCP Server Package Manifest
description: D-094: an MCP server is the registrable asset, not a single tool. Replaces mcp-tool-manifest, whose unit (one manifest = one tool) could not express a server at all — the server alias and endpoint lived only in a hand-edited office-profile.json, so tools were governed by review and audit while the server they ran on was not. The declared_tools[] entries here are the approval-time snapshot of the server's own `tools/list` response, annotated with the governance metadata the protocol does not carry (MCP has no authorization model: no roles, no classification, no rate limit, no audit). Those annotations are assigned by the reviewer at approval time and are never read from the server, which is untrusted by construction.

server_alias.description: Stable identifier for this server within the deployment. Lowercase kebab-case so it is safe as a log field, an audit key and a UI label without escaping. Replaces the hand-written alias in office-profile.json's allowed_mcp_servers — that list becomes a value derived from approved assets rather than an independently edited file.

provenance.description: INTERNAL: built in this organization, source reviewable here. THIRD_PARTY: obtained from outside. This is not a trust level the runtime acts on by itself — every server passes the same Policy Enforcement Point — but it is shown to the reviewer and the end user, who are entitled to know whose code is answering.
provenance.$comment: Deliberately not used to relax any check. A THIRD_PARTY server is not given fewer privileges than an INTERNAL one by this field alone; privileges come from declared_tools[].permissions, which a human assigns.

protocol_version.description: MCP protocolVersion this manifest was validated against, as returned by the server's `initialize` handshake (date-based, e.g. '2025-06-18'). Recorded so a client that negotiates a different version can say so instead of failing opaquely.

transport.description: How the client reaches this server. Exactly one of the two shapes below.

endpoint.description: Streamable HTTP endpoint. The only transport permitted in agent-runtime's `hosted` mode, because nothing is executed to reach it.

kind.description: D-094: permitted only in agent-runtime's `local` mode. Spawning a stdio child in `hosted` mode would run third-party code on a shared server under the audit context of whoever is currently chatting — a different risk class from D-084 (a file the user picked on their own PC). The client refuses STDIO registration in hosted mode structurally, not by configuration.

interpreter.description: Which configured interpreter runs the entrypoint. The absolute path comes from deployment settings, never from PATH lookup — the D-084 rule (`pythonInterpreterPath`, no `python`/`python3` guessing) applies here for the same reason: PATH resolution silently picks a different runtime than the one that was reviewed.

entrypoint.description: Path to the server's entry module, relative to the installed bundle root. Must stay inside the bundle: no absolute path, no '..' segment, no backslash or drive letter. There is no package-manager invocation here on purpose — `npx`, `uvx`, `pip install` and friends fetch and execute code at run time, which 구현 원칙 7 forbids and a closed network cannot do anyway. Dependencies are vendored into the bundle on a connected build machine.

args.description: Arguments passed to the entrypoint as an argv array — never a shell string, so no quoting or metacharacter interpretation exists to get wrong.

vendored_dependencies.description: Asserts that every runtime dependency ships inside the bundle. false means the server would need to reach a package registry at run time, which this deployment does not permit.

declared_tools.description: Approval-time snapshot of the server's `tools/list`, annotated with governance metadata. Replaces the hand-copied MCP_TOOL_SPECS in agent-runtime: `tools/list` is the authoritative source for names and input schemas, so the copy that used to drift (and needed 16 contract tests to hold it in place) no longer exists.

tool_name.description: Identifier-style name as reported by `tools/list`. Dot-separated namespacing allowed (05-mcp-security-governance.md §5); each segment is identifier-only — no path separators, no leading digit or dot.

label.description: Short human-readable purpose, shown in confirmation dialogs and used as TOOL_ROUTE candidate context (D-083).

input_schema.description: JSON Schema for tool input, as reported by `tools/list`. Validated before dispatch; a tool whose input cannot be validated is not callable.

risk_level.description: READ_ONLY has no side effects. WRITE does. D-094 relaxes 구현 원칙 8 to admit WRITE, because most third-party servers have write tools — but a WRITE tool is never offered to the LLM as a TOOL_ROUTE candidate and always requires explicit user confirmation.
risk_level.$comment: There is deliberately no `llm_routable` field. Whether a tool can be selected by the model is derived from risk_level by the Policy Enforcement Point, so 'WRITE but auto-routable' is not a state this contract can express. D-083's fail-closed design assumes a READ_ONLY-only surface; deriving rather than declaring is what keeps that assumption true.

permissions.description: 05-mcp-security-governance.md §7. Assigned by the reviewer, never read from the server. Default Deny: an empty allowed_roles or allowed_orgs denies everyone — it does not mean 'unrestricted'. allowed_sites is the one optional dimension; omitted or empty means 'not site-restricted'.

data_classification.description: Highest classification this tool's results may carry. Omitted means the server manifest's own classification applies.

confirmation_policy.description: When the user must confirm before dispatch. Three values, not a boolean — the previous manifest had only `requires_user_confirmation`, which could not express office-mcp-server's actual ON_PARAMETER policy and forced a lossy round-up (D-049). A WRITE tool may not declare NEVER.
confirmation_policy.$comment: Enforced by the PEP, which never lowers a policy below what the server itself declares.

execution_guards.description: 05-mcp-security-governance.md §8. Applied by the client, so they hold even for a server that ignores its own limits.

allOf.$comment: A WRITE tool cannot be dispatched without asking. NEVER would let a side-effecting call happen with no human in the loop, which is the specific thing 구현 원칙 8 existed to prevent before D-094 relaxed it.

tools_snapshot_hash.description: Hash of the `tools/list` response as seen at approval time. A server may legitimately change its tool list at run time (the protocol allows it), so the client re-hashes on connect and can tell 'the approved server' from 'a server that now offers something nobody reviewed'.

allOf.$comment: A stdio server is code this deployment will execute, so it must ship its dependencies. Leaving this to run time means a package fetch, which is both forbidden (구현 원칙 7) and impossible on a closed network.
